criteria.criterion: prepare <version> creates release/<version> from main, sets plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json's version (the version without its v) changing only that line, commits `Release <version>` as the branch's one commit, pushes the branch to origin, and opens a PR with gh titled `Release <version>` whose body is `notes <latest version tag> main`.
criteria.evidence: prepare.go openRelease: switch -c from main, regex replace of the first version, one commit, push, gh pr create with title and notes(latest,main); open_test.go asserts one commit, numstat 1/1, subject, title and body

criteria.criterion: On success stdout ends with exactly `prepared release/<version>: <PR url>` and `squash-merge it, then: go run ./tools/release publish <version>`; exit 0.
criteria.evidence: prepare.go prints both lines, exit 0; the test compares stdout exactly

criteria.criterion: The tool never merges, never pushes or commits to main and never tags. Any of those is a violation.
criteria.evidence: openRelease pushes only the release branch, commits on the branch, no tag or merge; the test asserts main and origin main are unchanged

criteria.criterion: The tool's tests use stubs for gh, go and claude on PATH and a local bare repository as origin, in temporary directories with a temporary HOME, addressed with git -C; no test runs the real gh, go install from the network, or this repository's origin.
criteria.evidence: open_test.go uses the prepared helper with STUBS on PATH, a stub gh, a bare origin and git(dir) which is git -C

criteria.criterion: Committed tests, run by the checks, cover the branch, its single commit and diff, the push to a local bare origin, the PR title and body given to a stub gh, and the output.
criteria.evidence: open_test.go TestPrepareOpensRelease covers each; checks go exit 0
